newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid extends rise on oil, gas, weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid extends rise on oil, gas, weather.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices on Thursday extended its Wednesday gains on stronger crude oil and natural gas prices, and cold weather in much of the eastern U.S.
"We're seeing firmer prices today," said an East Coast trader, adding tight supply and strength in bunker demand also bolstered the market.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent sulphur grade rose to $20.75-$21.25, up from Wednesday's $20.00-20.25 a barrel. December paper climbed to $21.30-$21.40 after reaching as high as $21.60, compared with $21.00-$20.25.
All NYH fuel oil values increased today following two reported sales Wednesday of 2.2 percent grade at $20.25.
"It's colder than average in the Northeast. It'll help demand a little bit," said another East Coast trader.
At the U.S. Gulf, fuel oil values were assessed higher in tandem with continued rise in NYH.
Limited supply and strong demand for high-sulphur material also pushed Gulf grades higher, traders said.
"There's very good demand right now from off-shore tankers," a Gulf Coast trader said.
Gulf Coast one-percent finished at $18.25-$18.75, up 50 cents from $17.75-$18.25 on Wednesday.
USG December three percent paper rose as well, now notationally assessed near $18.00, compared with Wednesday's bids at $17.50.
New York City gate swing gas surged to the $3.70-$3.80 area versus one percent resid at a $3.33/mmBtu equivalent. Today's city gas price compared with Wednesday's $3.55.
NYMEX December crude oil futures settled at $24.41, up 29 cents per barrel
